title: NSF Engines Development Award: Advancing manufacturing technologies (OH)
abstract:
This Regional Innovation Engines Development Award is focused on research-driven discovery, development, translation, and commercialization of sustainable manufacturing technologies essential for both production and products. The project fills a vital gap in the nation's ecosystem for problem-solving research, manufacturing output, robust supply chain management, livable wage jobs and opportunity structures, and socio-environmental stewardship. Northeast Ohio was the nation's manufacturing powerhouse, but poorly aligned institutions and unsustainable manufacturing practices have left a legacy of disinvestment, inequity, and environmental hazards across the region's 18 urban, suburban, and rural counties. The region of service extends across Northeast Ohio to create a robust network of industry, government entities, community groups, and leading research and academic institutions committed to problem-solving use-inspired research, innovation, technology translation, and workforce development. Led by Case Western Reserve University, the project's leadership includes Greater Cleveland Partnership, Team NEO, MAGNET, JumpStart, City of Cleveland, Cuyahoga County, Cleveland State University, Cleveland Water Alliance, Northeast Ohio Hispanic Center for Economic Development, and Urban League of Greater Cleveland.

The award efforts will focus on the creation of a robust, cooperative, aligned, and equitable framework for the substantial elevation of discovery and adoption of solutions in energy science, electrochemistry, green steel and chip production, carbon capture, storage/sequestration, and utilization, as well as alternatives to petroleum-based plastics, packaging, and biodegradable byproducts. We seek to reduce embodied energy, energy, and water usage, greenhouse emissions, all while transitioning to material circularity and sustainable energy, including process electrification. Robust and equitable job and opportunity structure creations are fundamental and woven into every activity. The planning effort will be driven through four integrated workstreams: Technology Innovation (problem-solving use-inspired research), Technology Adoption (translation, commercialization, adoption, Workforce and Talent Development (pathways, programs, pipelines), and Intentional Leadership and Governance (equity-focused leadership and governance). This award will prepare the region for an NSF Engine and an equitable and vibrant ecosystem that catalyzes innovation, accelerates sustainable technologies' translation, and develops a broader, more diverse workforce.
outcomes_report:
This project is aimed at nothing less than making Northeast Ohio the national leader in advanced materials and manufacturing. We brought together leading people and organizations from across the region, working together to design and build consensus for a strategic roadmap that will boost job growth, create new opportunities for everyone, elevate prosperity, and strengthen the nation's security and economy. Case Western Reserve University led the effort.

Northeast Ohio is home to 4.3 million people, but many face economic challenges. The average income is below $58,000, and nearly 200,000 residents live in areas where poverty rates are very high, especially in cities like Cleveland, Youngstown, Akron, and Canton. These cities were once at the heart of America's industrial boom but have since faced job losses and environmental issues. Rural communities also struggle with fewer job opportunities and limited access to innovation.

Despite these challenges, manufacturing remains a cornerstone of the region's economy. Ohio is the third-largest manufacturing state in the country, with more than 7,700 manufacturing facilities in Northeast Ohio alone. As shown in Figure 1, the region's location along the Great Lakes provides access to fresh water and shipping routes, making it a strategic place for industry.

Our project brought together leaders from business, universities, non-profits, philanthropy, and government. We organized our work into four main teams, focusing on: Leadership & Governance, Technology Innovation, Technology Adoption, and Workforce & Talent Development. Each team included experts from across the region, meeting regularly to drive progress.

We identified three main areas where Northeast Ohio is especially strong: Polymers, Chemicals & Coatings, and Metals (Figure 2). These clusters represent unique regional strengths in research, industry, and workforce. These clusters have since influenced regional economic development activities, including specific strategies to attract manufacturers to build new factories on redeveloped brownfield sites in Cleveland and Akron. The clusters are also inter-connected and synergistic, allowing technological advances in one area to rapidly accelerate advancement in related fields.

The team held four major workshops with hundreds of participants from local companies, universities, and organizations. These workshops focused on the three main clusters (Polymers, Chemicals & Coatings, Metals) as well as cross-cutting topics like advanced recycling and new, more sustainable materials. Participants identified real-world industry challenges that research can help solve, like making materials last longer, using more recycled content, and reducing environmental impacts.

The team developed a clear set of goals, which we call our "True North" objectives: a strong pipeline for materials innovation; expanded workforce opportunities; faster commercialization and market growth; and a connected, collaborative regional ecosystem (Figure 3). Thanks to these efforts, new research projects and partnerships have already begun, helping to turn ideas into real-world solutions.

To spread the word and engage more partners, we hosted events with national leaders in manufacturing, like Dr. Nabil Nasr from the REMADE Institute (Figure 4). These events helped expand our network and build excitement around the region's future in advanced manufacturing.

Our core team also completed a special training program from MIT, learning best practices from around the world to help guide our strategy and growth.

Because of the competitiveness of a Preliminary Proposal submitted in August 2024, our region was invited to submit a Full Proposal for the next phase of the NSF Regional Innovation Engine program. Our full proposal to begin building the engine, submitted in April 2025, included over 60 Letters of Collaboration from industry, government, and philanthropy, and more than 20 committed leaders. This momentum is helping to position Northeast Ohio as a national leader in advanced materials and manufacturing innovation.

This project has brought together people and organizations across Northeast Ohio, creating a shared vision for the region's economic future. By focusing on advanced materials and manufacturing, we are building new opportunities, attracting investment, and setting the stage for long-term success.
